## Active

### D-752 — the browser bundle is served by its own process, not a realm

> _2026-11-04 · core/blong-asset · active_

Firing a realm process to serve a suite's browser bundle gave the static surface the realm's
surface: its image, its service account, its dependencies and its route table. The bundle is now
served by core/blong-asset, a Deployment, Service and ConfigMap of its own, and the portal points
/s/ and an Exact / at it. The realm keeps a Prefix / for the paths only a process answers, which is
why portal.realm is optional rather than removed: a suite that needs /documentation still names one.
Serving files did not need the realm, but deleting the field would have broken every suite that
publishes a webhook or a documentation page on the same host.

### D-756 — the default script-src carries unsafe-eval

> _2026-11-04 · core/blong-asset · active_

The live portal failed to boot under script-src 'self': the framework's runtime compiles templates
with new Function, so the browser refused them and the page never rendered. 'unsafe-eval' is now in
the default policy, with a comment naming the reason; a suite with no such code can remove it
through csp.directives. Every other strict default (style-src inline, connect-src self,
frame-ancestors none, HSTS, permissions) was exercised by the live login and CRUD pages without a
violation.

### D-757 — document policies ride only on the shell

> _2026-11-04 · core/blong-asset · active_

A static server's headers are two sets: a document's policies (CSP, frame, referrer, permissions,
COOP, DNS prefetch, cross-domain) and a resource's own facts (nosniff, CORP, CORS, HSTS). Applying
the first to every script is work no browser does and a header list that reads as if each file were
a page. The server now sends only the resource facts on a subresource and a 404; the shell carries
both. HSTS stays on every answer because it is a policy of the host, not of the resource.
